name: Cold-cranking test of 12 V lead-acid and LFP starter batteries (EN 50342-1 pulse 9 A/Ah to 8 V, 10 s pause, 5.4 A/Ah to 6 V) at 0, -10, -18 and -30 C after 24 h cold soak, with C20 capacity at 25, 0 and -18 C
plain_name: Test whether a 12 V car starter battery can crank an engine at -30 C
description: Six 12 V starter batteries (two AGM lead-acid, 50 Ah and 92 Ah; four LFP packs) are soaked for 24 h in a climate chamber at the target temperature, then C20 capacity (25, 0, -18 C) and the EN 50342-1 cold-cranking pulse sequence (0, -10, -18, -30 C) are run inside the same chamber.
keywords: Test whether a 12 V car starter battery can crank an engine at -30 C

sources.citation: Bauknecht S. et al., Comparing the Cold-Cranking Performance of Lead-Acid and Lithium Iron Phosphate Batteries at Temperatures below 0 C, Batteries 2023, 9(3), 176, doi:10.3390/batteries9030176

reported_equipment: climate chamber (model not named in the retrieved text)

requirements.rationale: Capacity and cranking tests span 25 C (298.15 K) down to -30 C (243.15 K).
High-current discharge pulses are drawn from the battery while it sits in the chamber.
Optional: the chamber used held the test temperature with an accuracy of +/-0.25 C.
